verdict.rationale: React's docs show it renders components into a browser DOM node via createRoot and hydrateRoot. React also documents its own first-party React Developer Tools for inspecting components, props and state, so debugging rendered UI is supported. The evidence never explicitly says the output is plain DOM nodes inspectable in the browser's native devtools, and debugging relies on a separate DevTools extension. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that rendered output is real DOM inspectable in native browser devtools, any guidance on debugging via the browser Elements panel, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can debug my UI directly in browser devtools because the framework renders real DOM nodes

citations.quote: createRoot lets you create a root to display React components inside a browser DOM node.
hydrateRoot lets you display React components inside a browser DOM node whose HTML content was previously generated by react-dom/server.
Use React Developer Tools to inspect React components, edit props and state, and identify performance problems.
